root_causes.description: product-catalog server-side latency is pinned at the 10s ceiling (p50 and p99 both ~10000ms) and it is the only slow dependency common to the saturated callers checkout, frontend and recommendation. No errors, CPU, memory or restart anomalies are present, indicating injected/propagated latency rather than resource exhaustion or crashes.

evidence.expected_baseline: p99 latency < 50ms (leaf service, matches peer leaves currency/payment at ~2ms)
no CPU saturation; rules out cpu_stress

root_causes.description: recommendation is saturated (p50 ~7235ms, p99 ~10000ms). It calls product-catalog, so its latency is most plausibly downstream propagation, but it cannot be fully excluded as an independent latency source.

checkout p99 reaches the 10s cap. Since checkout only depends on cart/payment/email/shipping/currency (all normal) plus product-catalog, its latency is best explained by product-catalog; listed as a lower-confidence alternative for completeness.

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog for injected/sidecar network latency (e.g. tc/netem delay) or a slow flagd-driven fault and remove it.
Check product-catalog pod resource limits and CPU throttling (container_cpu_cfs_throttled) and raise limits or scale replicas if throttled.
Roll back the most recent product-catalog deployment/config change if the latency spike correlates with a rollout.
Add/adjust client-side timeouts and circuit breakers in frontend, checkout and recommendation so a slow product-catalog does not saturate upstream p99.
Verify recovery by re-checking product-catalog p99 latency against its <50ms baseline and confirming frontend/checkout/recommendation p99 returns to normal.
